items.summary: The ballot statement PDF could not be opened; a search-engine summary of it reports a claim of billions to keep Muni, BART and Caltrain running, exact wording unseen. Record: the June 2023 state budget deal, negotiated by the governor and legislators, gave transit agencies statewide $5.1 billion over four years with accountability measures; CalMatters said the Legislature proposed $1.1 billion more after the governor’s May plan offered no transit aid, and described Wiener as leading the charge to fend off the transit fiscal cliff. The June 2025 budget authorized a $750 million Bay Area transit loan, terms unsettled in September 2025; Mission Local wrote in October 2026 that Wiener secured an emergency state loan in 2025. Final loan terms not found; no state budget document could be opened.
items.title: State transit funding in the 2023 budget agreement and the 2025 Bay Area transit loan

citations.locator: Candidate statement of Scott Wiener, U.S. Representative, District 11 (claim on keeping Muni, BART and Caltrain running)

citations.quote: Transit agencies will receive a total of $5.1 billion over four years, though the money will be subject to accountability measures and state oversight.

While Newsom’s May budget proposal failed to provide any assistance for transit agencies facing a “fiscal cliff,” and delayed $2 billion in construction projects, the Legislature rejected that move and proposed an additional $1.1 billion over the next three years from the state’s cap-and-trade funds.

Sen. Scott Wiener, a Democrat from San Francisco who has been leading the charge to fend off the transit “fiscal cliff,” said the deal would cover a significant portion of transit systems’ collective operating deficit, but said the state should use more federal highway money to fund transit operations.

According to state legislation passed in June, the $750 million loan is cemented into the budget, but the duration and terms of the loan are to be determined in separate “budget trailing” legislation.

Eventually, just before adjournment, Newsom said he would “offer short-term financial assistance to support Bay Area transit agencies with hundreds of millions of dollars,” but he didn’t give an exact number.
In 2025, for instance, Wiener secured an emergency state loan for Muni, BART and Caltrain, intended to stabilize them until the regional transit measures passes.
